top3.title: S5. Perron-Frobenius vector = steady-state bit-density operator
top3.why: Perron-Frobenius eigenvector (phi, 1) of transfer matrix A; eigenvalue phi governs bit-density scaling via phi^{-k}. Both OpenAI and owner apply matrix eigenvalues to characterize recurrent system behavior.
top3.ruling_reason: Not level 3. None of the owner's specific objects appear in family 007 (ordinary two-point Chowla and binary corrected Elliott): no Perron-Frobenius eigenvector (phi,1), no eigenvalue phi, no matrix [[1,1],[1,0]], no stationary density. A grep of every TeX source finds no 'eigen', 'Perron' or 'Fibonacci', and the Lean comparators only cover Liouville and multiplicative correlation sums. The claim that the family uses 'matrix eigenvalues to characterize recurrent system behavior' is wrong; its 'recurrence constraints' are congruences on prime labels. What does overlap is the kind of structure. The family's nonbacktracking-moment theorem (quantitative/04-paths-trace.tex Thm q:trace; 07-spectral.tex Prop q:spectral) bounds the spectral radius of a transfer-type operator H_{d,d'}=1_{d!=d'}A_{d'}, whose powers record constrained paths, using rho(H)^{2k} <= ||H^k||_HS^2, a sum over closed words. The owner section (S5 plus its mapping tables) treats A^n, tr(A^n)=L_n and the dominant eigenvalue as the per-step growth factor. So both use the spectral radius, powers and traces of a path-transfer matrix, but share no specific object. H is signed (centered factors 1_{p|n}-1/p), so Perron-Frobenius does not apply to it, and the family never uses an eigenvector. That makes it level 2, and a weak one. The family's theorem says nothing about the owner item, so level 4 fails.

top3.title: [V] Entropy-rate law (spine)
top3.why: s = ln(lambda_max(A)) for any constrained system. Shared object: both use dominant eigenvalue to characterize entropy and growth rate of linear recurrences.
top3.ruling_reason: The owner's identity s = lim (1/n) ln Omega(n) = ln lambda_max(A) (the topological-entropy / Perron-Frobenius equality for constrained systems) does not appear in family 007. Nor does any 'dominant eigenvalue characterizing growth of linear recurrences'; the family has no linear recurrences. The kind of structure does match. In 04-paths-trace.tex the operator H=1_{d!=d'}A_{d'} has powers that enumerate paths with unequal consecutive tuples and with prohibited words deleted, and its spectral radius is bounded by the growth rate of a closed-word sum, rho(H)^{2k} <= ||H^k||_HS^2 <= [K(C_2 sqrt W)^J]^{2k}. The family also uses 'entropy' in the sense of log path-encoding counts (qualitative/paths.tex L268; trace-count.tex eq:trace-exceptional-entropy). That is the same kind of link between spectral radius and exponential growth of constrained path counts, so level 2. It is not level 3: the family has only a one-sided, finite-k inequality for a different, signed, weighted operator, with no limit identity and no Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue equality, so no specific identity or object is shared. The Chowla/Elliott theorem does not apply to entropy rates, so level 4 fails.

top3.why: Both center on phi: family uses continued fractions of pi via Diophantine theory; owner uses base-phi representation and log_phi (=log(phi)) as core operator for bit-density scaling and rapidity.
top3.ruling_reason: The premise 'both center on phi' is false. Family 017 is about pi, and its paper has zero hits for golden, Fibonacci or the Greek phi; the 'phi' strings in it are the name Philippon. The proof is a multivariable interpolation-determinant and zero-estimate argument (Laurent, Roth, Philippon) on logarithmic curves, not continued fractions. The paper says outright that exponent 2 is different from bounded continued-fraction partial quotients, and convergents of pi appear only in a footnote and a side remark. WIKI.md L140-200 covers base-phi log-space representation, the Focus Identity L(k-1)+L(k+1) = 5F(k), Zeckendorf uniqueness of the combined address, and register width growing as log_phi(S_max). That is numeration in base phi with no rational approximation, so there is no shared structure and no shared object. The only overlap is thematic: an irrational constant and logarithms.

top3.title: phi^{-1} integer approximation (5C/8)
top3.why: Directly addresses Diophantine approximation of phi^{−1}; family proves irrationality exponent via continued-fraction approximation, sharing the Diophantine approximation framework.
top3.ruling_reason: The analogy holds. The family bounds how well rationals p/q approximate pi (|pi - p/q| >= q^-nu for every nu > 2 and large q). The owner item is a rational approximant to an irrational: 5/8 for phi^-1, with its error. 5/8 = F5/F6 is in fact a continued-fraction convergent of phi^-1 with |phi^-1 - 5/8| < 1/(sqrt5 * 8^2), though the owner text does not say so. Level 3 fails because no specific object appears in both. The family's object is mu(pi) = 2 and its denominator-dependent bound. The owner states one dyadic approximant with a relative error and never relates the error to the denominator or to any exponent. The family's theorem is about pi only and says nothing about phi^-1. The claimed mechanism is also wrong: the family uses interpolation determinants, not continued-fraction approximation. Separate defect: the owner file states 'phi^-1 = psi+1', which is false. psi+1 = psi^2 = phi^-2, and the correct identity is phi^-1 = -psi = phi - 1.

Lines L451-511 of the owner doc analyse the 2x2 transfer matrix A=[[1,1],[1,0]] by its spectrum: the Perron-Frobenius density phi^{-k}, log_phi rapidity, the 13C/32 annealing sum, the F(W+2) count of fibbinary words, A as a permutation of a finite set, and the conserved sum I-1. Family 044 is about Nakajima varieties X = mu^{-1}(0)^{nu-stable}/G, the BFN Coulomb branch A_F, equivariant cohomology, and the scheme-theoretic fixed locus C[Y^nu] = A_F/<(A_F)_m : m != 0> (manuscript eq. 1.5). The manuscript never mentions Perron-Frobenius, Fibonacci, the golden ratio, a transfer matrix, or the spectrum of any recurrence matrix. Its only use of 'eigenvalue' is an aside: an endomorphism of an indecomposable quiver representation has a single eigenvalue. That has nothing to do with the owner's spectral analysis. The owner's 'period-1 fixed point' is a conserved quantity, not the fixed locus of a torus action. 'Lattice' means different things in the two texts: a finite set of words for the owner, O-lattices in the affine Grassmannian for the manuscript. A could be read as the adjacency matrix of a 2-vertex quiver with a loop, a case the Hikita theorem covers. Neither text makes that reading, and the theorem says nothing about A's spectrum or Fibonacci counts. The claim itself concedes 'different objects, same structural class' (matrices and rings), which is the 'algebra is not enough' case. Only vocabulary overlaps, so level 1.

Two overlapping words are homonyms. The owner's 'det' is det(A) = -1, while the manuscript's 'determinant stability' is the GIT character nu_det = sum_i det V_i. The owner's 'canonical-form quotient' is the Zeckendorf normal form, while the manuscript's quotients are GIT quotients and coefficient-algebra quotients. 'Lattice' and 'spectral' (spectral gap vs Borel spectral sequence) are homonyms too. The owner doc even says 'A^inf has no fixed point' (L137), whereas fixed subschemes and equivariant cohomology rings are what the family is about. Spectral algebra of a linear recurrence and the Hikita correspondence (symplectic duality, Coulomb branches) share nothing beyond being algebra. Only words overlap, so level 1.

A Poincare inequality Var(f) <= 2n^2<f,Lf> gives gap >= 1/(24n^2 C(n,4)), and that gives ||P^t(G,.) - pi||_TV <= (1/2)sqrt|Omega| e^{-gamma t}, which is convergence to a stationary law. The owner's A2 (L137-143) says the opposite: A expands, 'There is no equilibrium. The engine does not converge'. Its 'mixing property' is deterministic recurrence on the finite quotient (L141), which makes the map a permutation. In the family's framework a permutation has every eigenvalue on the unit circle, so its gap is zero and it never mixes: a point mass stays a point mass. The owner's 'spectral gap' (L185) belongs to a different operator, A acting on Z^2, which is not stochastic and has no stationary measure. manuscripts.title: Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields

plain: Deterministic polynomial-time algorithm factors every nonzero polynomial f∈F_p[x] completely (with multiplicities) using bit operations polynomial in (deg f+1) log p, without randomness or GRH.

top3.title: cascade
top3.why: cascade() function applies rewrite rules R1 (F(k)+F(k+1)=F(k+2)) and R3 (2F(k)=F(k+1)+F(k-2)) to reach canonical Zeckendorf form uniquely. Family 142 factors polynomials to unique irreducibles. Both are unique normal forms, both decidable in polynomial time, both decompose complex objects into indecomposable pieces.
top3.ruling_reason: The only thing the two texts share is a meta-property: a deterministic procedure that returns a unique canonical form. That is as generic as 'algebra' or 'a proof', so it does not reach level 2. The mathematical structures differ. Owner (zeck_kernel.py L234-373): an additive multiset rewriting system over Z. It uses the Fibonacci identities R1 F(k)+F(k+1)=F(k+2) and R3 2F(k)=F(k+1)+F(k-2), keeps the weighted mass sum F(k)*M(k) invariant, uses digit sum as a Lyapunov function, and gets uniqueness of the Zeckendorf normal form from local confluence plus Newman's lemma. Family 142: multiplicative factorization in F_p[x], built on the Berlekamp algebra, square-free decomposition via gcd(f,f'), Kummer extensions Y^q-F, divisors and places, a Hecke zero-free theorem and primitive roots. The 'indecomposable pieces' argument is false for the owner. Fibonacci terms are not atoms: R1 itself writes F(k+2) as F(k)+F(k+1). Zeckendorf uniqueness comes from the non-adjacency (fibbinary) constraint, not from irreducibility, and R1 merges terms upward, the opposite direction of factoring. The 'multiplicities' overlap is lexical only, and the roles are reversed. In the family the exponents e_i are part of the unique output. In the owner, multiplicities above 1 are transient and are eliminated (the final assert requires v==1). The polynomial-time argument is not in the owner text, which only has a PASS_CAP guard and a Lyapunov argument, and 'poly-time' is generic anyway. The local TeX source (math/preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/build/sections/*.tex) has 0 hits for fibonacci, lucas, zeckendorf, rewrit, confluen or newman across all 11 sections. Its only numeration-like object is Pohlig-Hellman base-q discrete-log digit extraction (02-finite-fields.tex L70-86), a cyclic-group step with no carries or rewriting normalization. The cascade never works mod p or with polynomials, so the family's theorem cannot apply to it. What remains is a loose thematic analogy (canonical decomposition, multiplicity bookkeeping): level 1.

Its theorems relate Hamming edit distance from H-freeness to copy density, and it disproves a polynomial removal bound. The owner item is a Zeckendorf number register that forbids the contiguous factor 11. The claimed shared structure rests on the word 'preserve'. In 190, 'order-preserving' describes the embedding maps. The fibbinary item has no embeddings, and 'preserves Fibonacci weight' is not order preservation. The two kinds of pattern containment also differ. Under 190's ordered-copy notion, the owner's own example N=10 -> 0b01001000 contains the all-ones pattern [1 1] at positions 3<6. So no-11 is a consecutive-factor constraint, not H-freeness in 190's sense, even in one dimension. The owner item has no edit distance, no copy count and no removal bound. The paper's only explicit binary encoding (eta_b(a) = floor(a/2^(5-b)) mod 2, which lists all 32 five-bit words in the anchor S) is plain base 2. It includes words with adjacent 1s, so it is explicitly not fibbinary. Shared vocabulary only, so level 1.

top3.why: ANALOGY: Both invoke determinants and eigenvalues of matrices as fundamental invariants. Owner: det(A^n)=(-1)^n and eigenvalues φ,ψ structure cascade system. Family: Fuglede-Kadison determinant of group-ring matrices. Parallel use of determinant as central invariant.
top3.ruling_reason: Words only: the shared item is the word 'determinant'. The family's object is the Fuglede-Kadison determinant. It is the exponential of a log-integral taken against the spectral measure in the group von Neumann algebra of an infinite non-sofic group G. It is always nonnegative, so it carries no sign. The owner's L36 section uses the ordinary signed determinant of the 2x2 integer matrix A = [[1,1],[1,0]]. Its whole point is the sign: det(A^n) = (-1)^n, read as the Cassini parity bit. For the trivial group, the Fuglede-Kadison determinant reduces to |det|. That equals 1 for every A^n, so it erases exactly the information the owner relies on. The owner's A lies in M_2(Z). That ring is directly finite because it is finite-dimensional, and A's Fuglede-Kadison determinant is 1, which satisfies the conjectured bound of at least 1. So none of the three refuted conjectures (Kaplansky direct finiteness, Gottschalk surjunctivity, the Determinant Conjecture) is nontrivial for the owner's object. The family text never mentions eigenvalues. A grep of the owner doc finds no group ring, von Neumann algebra, sofic group or cellular automaton. The only genuine bridge would be the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of xI - A over Z[Z]. That equals the Mahler measure of x^2 - x - 1, which is phi, and its log is the owner's spine entropy ln(phi). Neither text states this, and it sits on the amenable side where the Determinant Conjecture holds, so the family's counterexample still does not transfer.

top3.title: 4.3 Axis 2 — shell-index hand: `log_phi` rapidity, density `phi^{-k}`
top3.why: Theorem 4.3 states shell index is log_phi rapidity with Perron-Frobenius density phi^{-k}, the dominant eigenvector of transfer matrix A. This is exactly the eigenvalue/eigenvector machinery that Family 369 applies to Neumann operator.
top3.ruling_reason: Family 369 proves that every eigenfunction for the first POSITIVE Neumann eigenvalue of the Laplacian on a smooth simply connected planar domain has nonvanishing interior gradient. That eigenfunction is mean-zero and sign-changing: it is the mode after the constant ground state, not a Perron/dominant vector. The proof in the manuscript (build/sections/02-06) uses Filonov's mu<lambda_D, conformal reduction to the disk, Rohleder's div/curl vector variational principle, Green/Poisson boundary kernels for a disk potential, and McCullough-Quiggin reciprocal matrices with at most one positive eigenvalue. It never uses Perron-Frobenius for nonnegative matrices or dominant-eigenvector asymptotics. Its only ground-state positivity fact is a nonnegative Dirichlet minimizer, used once in the mu<lambda_D lemma to build mean-zero test functions; that is auxiliary, not shared structure. So the premise 'exactly the same eigen machinery' is false. Theorem 4.3 is the Perron vector of the 2x2 nonnegative primitive matrix A=[[1,1],[1,0]] plus a log_phi coordinate and fibbinary lacunarity. It has no differential operator, domain, boundary condition, critical point or extremum location. Because A is 2x2, its Perron vector (phi,1) has two components; 'components decay as phi^{-k} along the shell axis' is an interpretation, not an eigenvector shape. The overlap is generic 'eigenvalue/eigenvector' vocabulary, so this is level 1 (words).

top3.title: Implications for v013
top3.why: Discusses transfer matrix eigenvalues (phi, psi) and their role in determining spectral gap and correlations. Eigenvalue structure is shared with Family 369's Neumann eigenvalue analysis, though applied to different operators.
top3.ruling_reason: The shared terms name different objects. In the 369 manuscript, 'spectral gap' means Lemma lem:gap, mu < lambda_D: the first positive Neumann eigenvalue lies strictly below the first Dirichlet eigenvalue (Friedlander-Filonov, proved with plane-wave test functions). The theorem itself is about critical points and boundary extrema of the Neumann eigenfunction. L153 (Implications for v013 plus the tensor-hop addendum) uses 'spectral gap' in the transfer-matrix sense: the dominant eigenvalue phi against psi of A=[[1,1],[1,0]] controls correlation decay, read through a tight-binding / matrix-product-state analogy. Its 'boundary conditions' row means fixed end bits of a 1D shell lattice, not a Neumann condition. The owner side has no differential operator, eigenfunction, gradient, critical point or extremum statement. The claim's own 'applied to different operators' concedes there is no shared structure, so the overlap is vocabulary only: level 1. Side finding: the table row 'Spectral gap: phi - |psi| = sqrt5' is wrong, because phi - |psi| = 1 while phi - psi = sqrt5.

top3.title: S5. Perron-Frobenius vector = steady-state bit-density operator
top3.why: Section S5 on Perron-Frobenius vector as steady-state bit-density operator. Same use of dominant eigenvector for asymptotic behavior as Family 369 applies to Neumann eigenfunctions.
top3.ruling_reason: The claimed parallel ('dominant eigenvector for asymptotic behavior, same as 369 applies to Neumann eigenfunctions') does not hold for 369. Its eigenfunctions belong to the first positive Neumann eigenvalue, so they are orthogonal to the constant (the Neumann ground state, eigenvalue 0) and change sign. The theorem is a static result: the gradient never vanishes in the interior and the extrema lie on the boundary. It is not an asymptotic density, and no Perron-Frobenius argument appears in the proof, which uses conformal reduction, a vector variational principle, boundary kernels and reciprocal-matrix inertia. S5 reads the Perron vector (phi,1) of the 2x2 nonnegative matrix A as a ratio table for phi^{-k} bit density (ratio phi per shell, phi^n = F_n*phi + F_{n-1}). It contains no differential operator, domain, boundary condition or eigenfunction geometry. Its 'strictly decreasing in k' profile is an asserted exponential envelope, not a nonvanishing-gradient theorem for an eigenfunction. The overlap is 'eigenvector/eigenvalue' vocabulary only, so this is level 1.
